objects.description: Defines a Speex codec mode description and its function table. Holds identifiers, bitstream version, a pointer to mode-specific data, and function pointers for encoder/decoder init/destroy, encode/decode, and ctl, plus a query callback. Used to select and operate a particular narrowband/wideband/ultra-wideband mode.

Forward declaration of SpeexMode. The full definition appears later in the header via typedef struct SpeexMode { ... } SpeexMode; This declaration alone is incomplete and not constructible; included here for completeness of defined types in this header.
Function pointer type for encoder state initialization. Returns an opaque encoder state for a given SpeexMode.
Function pointer type for destroying a previously created encoder state.
Function pointer type for the core frame encoding routine. Encodes one frame from input buffer to SpeexBits.
Function pointer type for encoder control (ioctl-like) operations.
Function pointer type for decoder state initialization for a given SpeexMode.
Function pointer type for destroying a previously created decoder state.
Function pointer type for the core frame decoding routine. Decodes one frame from SpeexBits into an output buffer.
Function pointer type for decoder control (ioctl-like) operations.

objects.definition: typedef int (*mode_query_func)(const void *mode, int request, void *ptr);
objects.description: Function pointer type to query mode-specific information, used by SpeexMode::query.

objects.definition:
typedef struct SpeexBits {
   char *chars;   /**< "raw" data */
   int   nbBits;  /**< Total number of bits stored in the stream*/
   int   charPtr; /**< Position of the byte "cursor" */
   int   bitPtr;  /**< Position of the bit "cursor" within the current char */
   int   owner;   /**< Does the struct "own" the "raw" buffer (member "chars") */
   int   overflow;/**< Set to one if we try to read past the valid data */
   int   buf_size;/**< Allocated size for buffer */
   int   reserved1; /**< Reserved for future use */
   void *reserved2; /**< Reserved for future use */
} SpeexBits;
objects.description: Bit-packing data structure for Speex bit-streams. Holds the buffer, current bit/byte cursors, ownership flag, overflow status, and buffer size. Used for reading/writing packed bits during encode/decode. reserved1/reserved2 are placeholders for future extension.

Function pointer type for Speex in-band callback handlers. Implementations read parameters from the provided SpeexBits stream and act on the supplied codec/decoder state and user data. Returns an int status code.

Structure describing a single in-band callback registration: the callback identifier, the handler function, and opaque user data passed to the handler. Also contains reserved fields for future ABI extension.
Forward declaration of the Speex codec mode descriptor. Only referenced here to allow speex_init_header() to take a mode; the actual structure is defined elsewhere. Details unknown in this header.

objects.definition:
typedef struct SpeexHeader {
   char speex_string[SPEEX_HEADER_STRING_LENGTH];   /**< Identifies a Speex bit-stream, always set to "Speex   " */
   char speex_version[SPEEX_HEADER_VERSION_LENGTH]; /**< Speex version */
   spx_int32_t speex_version_id;       /**< Version for Speex (for checking compatibility) */
   spx_int32_t header_size;            /**< Total size of the header ( sizeof(SpeexHeader) ) */
   spx_int32_t rate;                   /**< Sampling rate used */
   spx_int32_t mode;                   /**< Mode used (0 for narrowband, 1 for wideband) */
   spx_int32_t mode_bitstream_version; /**< Version ID of the bit-stream */
   spx_int32_t nb_channels;            /**< Number of channels encoded */
   spx_int32_t bitrate;                /**< Bit-rate used */
   spx_int32_t frame_size;             /**< Size of frames */
   spx_int32_t vbr;                    /**< 1 for a VBR encoding, 0 otherwise */
   spx_int32_t frames_per_packet;      /**< Number of frames stored per Ogg packet */
   spx_int32_t extra_headers;          /**< Number of additional headers after the comments */
   spx_int32_t reserved1;              /**< Reserved for future use, must be zero */
   spx_int32_t reserved2;              /**< Reserved for future use, must be zero */
} SpeexHeader;
objects.description: Struct describing the Ogg/Speex stream header fields. Used to create or parse the header packet for file-based formats (not needed for RTP-only usage). Fields encode versioning, sample rate, mode, channels, bitrate, frame sizing, VBR flag, and counts. reserved1/2 must be zero. Memory for instances is typically stack- or user-allocated; helper APIs exist to initialize and serialize/deserialize.

Opaque-but-exposed state carrier for Speex intensity stereo processing. Holds balance, energy ratio, smoothed per-channel gains, and two reserved fields. Used by encode/decode helpers to carry smoothing and mixing state across frames.

functions.name: speex_encoder_init
functions.description: Create and return a new Speex encoder state for the specified mode (e.g., speex_nb_mode, speex_wb_mode). One encoder state is required per audio channel. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: mode must point to a valid SpeexMode (e.g., &speex_nb_mode, &speex_wb_mode, or &speex_uwb_mode).
Create one state per channel if encoding multiple channels.
The returned state must be destroyed with speex_encoder_destroy when no longer needed.
Do not use the state after destruction.

functions.name: speex_encoder_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and free all resources associated with an existing Speex encoder state.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex encoder state previously returned by speex_encoder_init.
Do not call this function more than once for the same state.
Do not use the encoder state after calling this function.

functions.name: speex_encode
functions.description: Encode one frame of PCM audio from a float buffer using an existing Speex encoder state, writing the encoded bitstream to bits. Returns 0 if the frame need not be transmitted (DTX only), 1 otherwise. Note: the encoder may overwrite the input buffer; treat it as uninitialized after the call.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex encoder state created by speex_encoder_init.
in must point to a frame of PCM samples expected in the ±2^15 range (float).
in may be overwritten by the encoder and must be considered uninitialized after the call.
bits must be a valid, initialized SpeexBits object suitable for writing encoded data.
The number of samples in the input frame must match the encoder frame size (obtainable via speex_encoder_ctl with SPEEX_GET_FRAME_SIZE).
Check the return value: 0 indicates DTX/no transmission, 1 indicates an encoded frame is present in bits.

functions.name: speex_encode_int
functions.description: Encode one frame of 16-bit PCM audio using an existing Speex encoder state, writing the encoded bitstream to bits. Returns 0 if the frame need not be transmitted (DTX only), 1 otherwise.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex encoder state created by speex_encoder_init.
in must point to a frame of 16-bit PCM samples with a ±2^15 range (spx_int16_t).
bits must be a valid, initialized SpeexBits object suitable for writing encoded data.
The number of samples in the input frame must match the encoder frame size (obtainable via speex_encoder_ctl with SPEEX_GET_FRAME_SIZE).
Check the return value: 0 indicates DTX/no transmission, 1 indicates an encoded frame is present in bits.

functions.name: speex_encoder_ctl
functions.description: Control or query encoder parameters via ioctl-like requests (SPEEX_* macros). Returns 0 on success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter. Used to set/get options such as quality, bitrate, VBR, frame size query, etc.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex encoder state created by speex_encoder_init.
request must be one of the defined SPEEX_* encoder/codec control macros (e.g., SPEEX_SET_QUALITY, SPEEX_GET_FRAME_SIZE, SPEEX_SET_VBR, etc.).
ptr must point to a variable of the appropriate type for the given request (e.g., int*, float*, function pointer), or be NULL if the request does not require data.
Callers must handle return values: 0 for success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter.

functions.name: speex_decoder_init
functions.description: Create and return a new Speex decoder state for the specified mode (e.g., speex_nb_mode, speex_wb_mode). One decoder state is required per audio channel. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: mode must point to a valid SpeexMode (e.g., &speex_nb_mode, &speex_wb_mode, or &speex_uwb_mode).
Create one state per channel if decoding multiple channels.
The returned state must be destroyed with speex_decoder_destroy when no longer needed.
Do not use the state after destruction.

functions.name: speex_decoder_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and free all resources associated with an existing Speex decoder state.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex decoder state previously returned by speex_decoder_init.
Do not call this function more than once for the same state.
Do not use the decoder state after calling this function.

functions.name: speex_decode
functions.description: Decode one frame of speech using an existing Speex decoder state from the provided bitstream into a float PCM buffer. bits may be NULL to perform packet-loss concealment. Returns 0 on success, -1 on end of stream, and -2 for a corrupt stream.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex decoder state created by speex_decoder_init.
bits must be a valid, initialized SpeexBits object containing encoded data, or NULL if the packet was lost (to trigger PLC).
out must point to a buffer large enough to hold one decoded frame of float samples (frame size obtainable via speex_decoder_ctl with SPEEX_GET_FRAME_SIZE).
Callers must check the return value: 0 (success), -1 (end of stream), -2 (corrupt stream).

functions.name: speex_decode_int
functions.description: Decode one frame of speech using an existing Speex decoder state from the provided bitstream into a 16-bit PCM buffer. bits may be NULL to perform packet-loss concealment. Returns 0 on success, -1 on end of stream, and -2 for a corrupt stream.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex decoder state created by speex_decoder_init.
bits must be a valid, initialized SpeexBits object containing encoded data, or NULL if the packet was lost (to trigger PLC).
out must point to a buffer large enough to hold one decoded frame of 16-bit samples (frame size obtainable via speex_decoder_ctl with SPEEX_GET_FRAME_SIZE).
Callers must check the return value: 0 (success), -1 (end of stream), -2 (corrupt stream).

functions.name: speex_decoder_ctl
functions.description: Control or query decoder parameters via ioctl-like requests (SPEEX_* macros). Returns 0 on success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter. Used to set/get options such as enhancement, VBR-related info, high-pass filtering, frame size query, PLC tuning, etc.
requirements: state must be a valid Speex decoder state created by speex_decoder_init.
request must be one of the defined SPEEX_* decoder/codec control macros (e.g., SPEEX_SET_ENH, SPEEX_GET_FRAME_SIZE, SPEEX_GET_ACTIVITY, SPEEX_SET_HIGHPASS, etc.).
ptr must point to a variable of the appropriate type for the given request (e.g., int*, float*), or be NULL if the request does not require data.
Callers must handle return values: 0 for success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter.

functions.name: speex_mode_query
functions.signature: int speex_mode_query(const SpeexMode *mode, int request, void *ptr);
functions.description: Query information about a Speex mode via ioctl-like requests (SPEEX_MODE_* and related macros). Returns 0 on success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter.
requirements: mode must point to a valid SpeexMode (e.g., &speex_nb_mode, &speex_wb_mode, &speex_uwb_mode).
request must be a defined mode query macro (e.g., SPEEX_MODE_FRAME_SIZE, SPEEX_SUBMODE_BITS_PER_FRAME).
ptr must point to a variable of the appropriate type to receive the queried value.
Callers must handle return values: 0 for success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter.

functions.name: speex_lib_ctl
functions.description: Control or query global libspeex behavior via ioctl-like requests (SPEEX_LIB_* macros), such as retrieving version information. Returns 0 on success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter.
requirements: request must be one of the SPEEX_LIB_* macros (e.g., SPEEX_LIB_GET_MAJOR_VERSION, SPEEX_LIB_GET_VERSION_STRING).
ptr must point to a variable of the appropriate type for the given request.
Callers must handle return values: 0 for success, -1 for unknown request, -2 for invalid parameter.

functions.name: speex_lib_get_mode
functions.description: Obtain a pointer to one of the available Speex modes by mode ID (e.g., SPEEX_MODEID_NB, SPEEX_MODEID_WB, SPEEX_MODEID_UWB). On some platforms, mode ID SPEEX_MODEID_NB may be resolved directly to &speex_nb_mode via a macro.
requirements: mode must be a valid mode ID (e.g., SPEEX_MODEID_NB, SPEEX_MODEID_WB, SPEEX_MODEID_UWB).
The returned pointer refers to a statically defined SpeexMode; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: speex_bits_init
functions.description: Initializes and allocates resources for a SpeexBits struct so it can be used for packing/unpacking bits. Typical usage: declare a SpeexBits on the stack and call this before any read/write operations.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to a SpeexBits instance
Must be called before using other SpeexBits operations on this instance unless using speex_bits_init_buffer instead
Do not mix with speex_bits_init_buffer on the same instance without destroying/resetting first (implied by separate initialization paths)
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown

functions.name: speex_bits_init_buffer
functions.description: Initializes a SpeexBits struct to use a caller-provided preallocated buffer for internal storage. Use when you want to avoid internal allocation and control the memory buffer.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to a SpeexBits instance
buff must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least buf_size bytes
buf_size must be non-negative; zero-sized buffers are allowed but cannot store data
Do not free or reuse buff for other purposes while the SpeexBits instance is using it
Must not call speex_bits_init on the same instance after this without destroying/resetting first
Behavior if operations exceed buf_size is unspecified in this header; callers should ensure capacity is sufficient

functions.name: speex_bits_set_bit_buffer
functions.description: Configures an already-initialized SpeexBits to use data from an existing buffer (e.g., for decoding without copying). Primarily for reading/decoding from external memory.
requirements: bits must be initialized (via speex_bits_init or speex_bits_init_buffer) before calling
buff must be a non-null pointer to readable data of at least buf_size bytes
buf_size must be non-negative
The lifetime of buff must cover all subsequent reads from the SpeexBits instance
This function sets the bit buffer; exact ownership and writeability semantics are not fully documented—assume the buffer must remain valid and unmodified unless documented otherwise

functions.name: speex_bits_destroy
functions.description: Frees resources associated with a SpeexBits struct. Currently a no-op per comment, but may change; call it to future-proof code.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to a previously initialized SpeexBits instance
After destruction, the instance must not be used unless reinitialized
Safe to call exactly once per initialized instance; multiple destroys on the same instance are invalid

functions.name: speex_bits_reset
functions.description: Resets a SpeexBits instance to its initial post-initialization state, erasing any current content.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
All unread data in the stream is discarded
After reset, previous cursors/positions become invalid

functions.name: speex_bits_rewind
functions.description: Rewinds the bit cursor to the beginning of the current stream content for reading without erasing data.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance containing data
Only the read position changes; content must have been previously written or read in

functions.name: speex_bits_read_from
functions.signature: void speex_bits_read_from(SpeexBits *bits, const char *bytes, int len);
functions.description: Initializes or fills the bit-stream from a block of memory, setting the stream content to the provided bytes for subsequent reading.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
bytes must be a non-null pointer to at least len bytes of readable data
len must be non-negative
Existing content may be replaced; subsequent reads will consume from the provided data

functions.name: speex_bits_read_whole_bytes
functions.signature: void speex_bits_read_whole_bytes(SpeexBits *bits, const char *bytes, int len);
functions.description: Appends complete bytes to the bit-stream without bit-level packing (concatenates whole bytes). Useful when adding aligned data to the stream.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
bytes must be a non-null pointer to at least len bytes of readable data
len must be non-negative
Caller should ensure the internal buffer has sufficient capacity; behavior on insufficient capacity is not specified here

functions.name: speex_bits_write
functions.description: Writes the current bit-stream content into a caller-provided buffer, up to max_len bytes. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
bytes must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least max_len bytes
max_len must be non-negative
Caller must check the return value to know how many bytes were actually written and to avoid using unwritten memory

functions.name: speex_bits_write_whole_bytes
functions.description: Writes only the complete-byte portion of the stream into the output buffer and removes those written bytes from the stream. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
bytes must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least max_len bytes
max_len must be non-negative
Caller must check the return value to determine how many bytes were written and removed from the stream

functions.name: speex_bits_pack
functions.signature: void speex_bits_pack(SpeexBits *bits, int data, int nbBits);
functions.description: Appends the lower nbBits of the integer data into the bit-stream at the current bit position.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
nbBits must be non-negative and should be within a reasonable bit-width of int (exact bounds unspecified)
Only the least-significant nbBits of data are used; higher bits are ignored
Caller should ensure sufficient internal capacity or buffer growth semantics; unspecified here

functions.name: speex_bits_unpack_signed
functions.description: Reads the next nbBits from the stream and interprets them as a signed integer, advancing the read cursor.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance containing at least nbBits bits available
nbBits must be non-negative
If reading past valid data occurs, the SpeexBits.overflow flag may be set (per struct field semantics); callers should avoid underflow by checking availability (e.g., speex_bits_remaining)

functions.name: speex_bits_unpack_unsigned
functions.description: Reads the next nbBits from the stream and interprets them as an unsigned integer, advancing the read cursor.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance containing at least nbBits bits available
nbBits must be non-negative
If reading past valid data occurs, the SpeexBits.overflow flag may be set; callers should avoid underflow by checking availability (e.g., speex_bits_remaining)

functions.name: speex_bits_nbytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes currently in the stream, including the last byte even if it is only partially filled.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance

functions.name: speex_bits_peek_unsigned
functions.description: Peeks at the next nbBits as an unsigned integer without advancing the cursor.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
nbBits must be non-negative
Caller should ensure at least nbBits bits are available to avoid overflow/undefined behavior

functions.name: speex_bits_peek
functions.description: Peeks at the next single bit in the stream (returns its value) without advancing the cursor.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
At least 1 bit should be available to avoid overflow/undefined behavior

functions.name: speex_bits_advance
functions.description: Advances the bit cursor position by n bits without returning data.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
n must be non-negative
Caller should ensure that advancing by n does not exceed the available bits to avoid overflow/invalid state

functions.name: speex_bits_remaining
functions.description: Returns the number of bits remaining that can still be read from the stream.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance

functions.name: speex_bits_insert_terminator
functions.description: Inserts a terminator into the stream so it can be sent as a packet with auto-detection of the number of frames. Typically used when finalizing packet boundaries.
requirements: bits must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SpeexBits instance
Should be called at an appropriate packet boundary; exact framing semantics are library-specific and not detailed here

functions.name: speex_inband_handler
functions.description: Parses and handles a single in-band request embedded in the Speex bitstream. It reads the request from bits and dispatches it to the appropriate registered callback in callback_list, passing state through. Typical usage: call this from a decoder after detecting/encountering an in-band signaling opcode in the stream to consume its payload and apply side effects (e.g., mode/VBR/enhancer changes, user-defined signals). Return value and exact error semantics are not documented here.
requirements: bits must point to a valid, initialized SpeexBits containing the next in-band request payload at the current read position
callback_list must point to a valid array/list of SpeexCallback entries (size and registration policy not specified here; SPEEX_MAX_CALLBACKS is defined as 16 in this header)
state must be a valid pointer to the decoder (or application-defined) context expected by the registered callbacks
Must be called only when the bitstream position corresponds to an in-band request; otherwise behavior is undefined/unknown
Caller must manage any return code (semantics not documented)

functions.name: speex_std_mode_request_handler
functions.description: Standard handler for a mode request: changes the codec mode without further validation (“no questions asked”). Intended to be invoked by the in-band handler when a mode change opcode is encountered.
requirements: bits must be positioned on the in-band payload for a mode request
state must be a valid decoder (or relevant) state object that supports changing mode
data is a user-supplied pointer passed at registration; meaning unspecified
Caller should only invoke this for the SPEEX_INBAND_MODE_REQUEST in-band item

functions.name: speex_std_high_mode_request_handler
functions.description: Standard handler for a high mode request: changes the high mode setting without validation. Used for in-band high-mode change signaling.
requirements: bits must be positioned on the in-band payload for a high mode request
state must be a valid decoder (or relevant) state object that supports changing the high mode
data is a user-supplied pointer passed at registration; meaning unspecified
Caller should only invoke this for the SPEEX_INBAND_HIGH_MODE_REQUEST in-band item

functions.name: speex_std_char_handler
functions.description: Standard handler for in-band characters: reads a character from bits and writes it to stderr. Intended for simple in-band text signaling.
requirements: bits must be positioned on the in-band payload for a character (SPEEX_INBAND_CHAR)
state is not used by the standard implementation (must still be a valid pointer)
data is a user-supplied pointer passed at registration; meaning unspecified
Caller should only invoke this for the SPEEX_INBAND_CHAR in-band item

functions.name: speex_default_user_handler
functions.description: Default handler for user-defined requests: ignores the request. Provides a safe no-op for unknown or user-defined in-band opcodes.
requirements: bits must be valid and positioned at the start of the user-defined in-band payload
state may be any pointer (not used by the default implementation)
data may be any pointer (not used by the default implementation)

functions.name: speex_std_low_mode_request_handler
functions.description: Standard handler for a low mode request: changes the low mode setting without validation. Used for in-band low-mode change signaling.
requirements: bits must be positioned on the in-band payload for a low mode request
state must be a valid decoder (or relevant) state object that supports changing the low mode
data is a user-supplied pointer passed at registration; meaning unspecified
Caller should only invoke this for the SPEEX_INBAND_LOW_MODE_REQUEST in-band item

functions.name: speex_std_vbr_request_handler

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: Provide interesting valid arbitrary binary data for Speex bits/stereo helpers.
# The fuzz stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for:
# - speex_bits_read_from / read_whole_bytes: arbitrary bytes become bitstream content
# - speex_encode_stereo/_int and decode_stereo/_int: they map seed bytes to sample values
# Goal: Generate bytes that are valid and exercise different behaviors: patterns, ramps,
# silence, max/min extremes, alternating signs, and embedded plausible Speex/Ogg header-like
# sequences to encourage varied code paths when treated as generic byte streams.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _chunk_header(tag: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Simple TLV-like wrapper: [tag(4)][len(2 LE)][payload]
    return tag[:4].ljust(4, b"\x00") + struct.pack('<H', len(payload)) + payload

def _make_ogg_speex_header() -> bytes:
    # Not a full Ogg page, but embed recognizable strings to tick any parsers
    speex_string = b"Speex   "  # 8 bytes per spec constant
    version = b"speex-1.2.1".ljust(20, b"\x00")  # typical field lengths vary; just embed
    # Build minimalistic SpeexHeader-like payload (little endian ints)
    rate = random.choice([8000, 16000, 32000])
    mode = random.choice([0, 1, 2])  # nb, wb, uwb
    mode_bv = 4
    nb_channels = random.choice([1, 2])
    bitrate = random.choice([0, 11000, 15000, -1])  # -1 unknown/auto
    frame_size = random.choice([160, 320, 640])
    vbr = random.choice([0, 1])
    fpp = random.choice([1, 2, 4])
    extra = 0
    reserved1 = 0
    reserved2 = 0
    header_size = 80  # sizeof-like placeholder
    fields = [
        1,              # speex_version_id
        header_size,
        rate,
        mode,
        mode_bv,
        nb_channels,
        bitrate,
        frame_size,
        vbr,
        fpp,
        extra,
        reserved1,
        reserved2,
    ]
    payload = speex_string + version + b"".join(struct.pack('<i', x) for x in fields)
    return _chunk_header(b"SPXH", payload)

def _pattern_bytes(length: int) -> bytes:
    # Alternating patterns exercise bit pack/unpack boundaries
    patterns: List[bytes] = [
        bytes([0x00]) * length,                      # silence / zeros
        bytes([0xFF]) * length,                      # all ones
        bytes([0x55]) * length,                      # 0101 pattern
        bytes([0xAA]) * length,                      # 1010 pattern
        bytes((i % 256 for i in range(length))),     # ramp up
        bytes(((255 - (i % 256)) for i in range(length))),  # ramp down
        bytes(((i * 31) & 0xFF for i in range(length))),    # pseudo-linear mix
    ]
    return random.choice(patterns)

def _stereo_like_block(frame_size: int, integer: bool) -> bytes:
    # Build 2*frame_size samples as bytes derived from plausible audio
    stereo_len = frame_size * 2
    # Make left a sine-ish table, right a phase-shifted variant to provoke energy ratio calc
    # We stay in bytes; consumers in stubs map to [-1,1] floats or small int deltas.
    # Keep within 0..255 domain.
    out = bytearray(stereo_len)
    # Choose amplitude ranges to cover extremes and small values
    amp = random.choice([16, 64, 127, 200])
    phase = random.choice([0, 32, 64, 96])
    for i in range(stereo_len):
        # simple triangle-like waveform using modular arithmetic
        t = (i + phase) % 256
        val = (amp - abs((t % 128) - 64)) * 2  # 0..~256
        b = max(0, min(255, val))
        out[i] = b
    # Interleave some extremes
    for i in range(0, stereo_len, max(1, stereo_len // 13)):
        out[i] = random.choice([0, 255, 128])
    return bytes(out)

def _mono_like_block(frame_size: int, integer: bool) -> bytes:
    # Mono of length frame_size; decode_* stubs read only first frame_size
    out = bytearray(frame_size)
    # Mix of silence, impulse, and small ramp
    mode = random.choice(["silence", "impulse", "ramp", "alt"]) 
    if mode == "silence":
        return bytes([128] * frame_size)
    if mode == "impulse":
        for i in range(frame_size):
            out[i] = 128
        pos = random.randrange(frame_size)
        out[pos] = random.choice([0, 255])
        return bytes(out)
    if mode == "ramp":
        for i in range(frame_size):
            out[i] = (i * 7) & 0xFF
        return bytes(out)
    # alt small values
    for i in range(frame_size):
        out[i] = 128 + (8 if (i & 1) == 0 else -8)  # around center
    return bytes(out)

def _compose_sections(sections: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    data = b"".join(sections)
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)

    # Decide overall size budget
    budget = random.randint(128, min(2048, MAX_SIZE))

    # Build multiple sections to cater to different stubs in one buffer
    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Embed a header-like chunk
    if random.random() < 0.8:
        sections.append(_make_ogg_speex_header())

    # 2) Add raw pattern region for bits_read_from/whole_bytes
    pat_len = random.randint(32, min(512, budget // 4 + 1))
    sections.append(_chunk_header(b"PAT0", _pattern_bytes(pat_len)))

    # 3) Add stereo-like block sized to small frame size used by stubs (<=256)
    frame = random.randint(1, 256)
    stereo_block = _stereo_like_block(frame, integer=False)
    sections.append(_chunk_header(b"STRF", stereo_block))

    # 4) Add integer-stereo-like block
    frame2 = random.randint(1, 256)
    stereo_block_i = _stereo_like_block(frame2, integer=True)
    sections.append(_chunk_header(b"STRI", stereo_block_i))

    # 5) Add mono-like blocks for decode_stereo paths
    mono_frame = random.randint(1, 256)
    sections.append(_chunk_header(b"MONF", _mono_like_block(mono_frame, integer=False)))
    mono_frame_i = random.randint(1, 256)
    sections.append(_chunk_header(b"MONI", _mono_like_block(mono_frame_i, integer=True)))

    # 6) Optional filler of whole-byte aligned random bytes
    if random.random() < 0.6:
        fill_len = random.randint(16, 256)
        sections.append(_chunk_header(b"FILL", random.randbytes(fill_len) if hasattr(random, 'randbytes') else bytes([random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(fill_len)])))

    data = _compose_sections(sections)

    # Ensure within budget and max size
    if len(data) > budget:
        data = data[:budget]

    return data

import struct
import random
import string

# Speex header constants per spec/reference implementation
SPEEX_HEADER_STRING = b"Speex   "  # 8 bytes including spaces
SPEEX_HEADER_VERSION = b"speex-1.2rc"  # canonical example; will pad/trim to 20 bytes
SPEEX_HEADER_STRING_LENGTH = 8
SPEEX_HEADER_VERSION_LENGTH = 20

# Mode IDs (as used by libspeex)
SPEEX_MODEID_NB = 0   # narrowband 8 kHz
SPEEX_MODEID_WB = 1   # wideband 16 kHz
SPEEX_MODEID_UWB = 2  # ultra-wideband 32 kHz

# Helper: choose sample rate consistent with mode
def pick_rate_for_mode(rng, mode):
    if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_NB:
        return rng.choice([8000, 11025, 12000])
    if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_WB:
        return rng.choice([16000, 22050, 24000])
    if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_UWB:
        return rng.choice([32000, 44100, 48000])
    # Fallback
    return 8000

# Helper: compute a plausible frame size for mode/rate
# Common frame sizes (samples) per channel: NB ~160, WB ~320, UWB ~640 for 20ms frames
def pick_frame_size(mode):
    if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_NB:
        return 160
    if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_WB:
        return 320
    if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_UWB:
        return 640
    return 160

# Helper: bitstream version (Speex uses 4 for 1.2 reference)
BITSTREAM_VERSION = 4

# Create a properly padded C-style char array field
def fixed_cstr(data: bytes, length: int) -> bytes:
    data = data[:length]
    if len(data) < length:
        data += b"\x00" * (length - len(data))
    return data

# Build a valid Speex header structure and serialize as per speex_header_to_packet() output
# The layout (little-endian 32-bit ints) after the two fixed strings is:
# int32 speex_version_id
# int32 header_size (sizeof(SpeexHeader))
# int32 rate
# int32 mode
# int32 mode_bitstream_version
# int32 nb_channels
# int32 bitrate
# int32 frame_size
# int32 vbr
# int32 frames_per_packet
# int32 extra_headers
# int32 reserved1 (0)
# int32 reserved2 (0)

def build_header_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose mode
    mode = rng.choice([SPEEX_MODEID_NB, SPEEX_MODEID_WB, SPEEX_MODEID_UWB])

    # Choose fields
    rate = pick_rate_for_mode(rng, mode)
    nb_channels = rng.choice([1, 2])

    # Bitrate hint: -1 for unknown/variable, or pick a typical kbps scaled by 1000
    # Speex uses bps; typical: NB 8000..15000, WB 11000..28000, UWB 18000..44000
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        bitrate = -1
    else:
        if mode == SPEEX_MODEID_NB:
            bitrate = rng.choice([8000, 11000, 12200, 15000])
        elif mode == SPEEX_MODEID_WB:
            bitrate = rng.choice([14000, 18000, 22000, 28000])
        else:
            bitrate = rng.choice([22000, 32000, 40000, 44000])

    frame_size = pick_frame_size(mode)
    vbr = rng.choice([0, 1])
    frames_per_packet = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4])
    extra_headers = rng.choice([0, 0, 0, 1, 2])

    # Strings
    # Keep the magic exactly as required
    speex_string = fixed_cstr(SPEEX_HEADER_STRING, SPEEX_HEADER_STRING_LENGTH)

    # Version string: vary slightly to exercise parser while staying valid
    base_versions = [
        b"speex-1.2rc",
        b"Speex 1.2",
        b"speex-1.1",
        b"speex-1.0",
    ]
    ver = rng.choice(base_versions)
    # Optionally append a short suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        suffix = (b"-" + bytes([ord('a') + rng.randrange(0, 6)]))
        ver = ver + suffix
    speex_version = fixed_cstr(ver, SPEEX_HEADER_VERSION_LENGTH)

    speex_version_id = BITSTREAM_VERSION
    mode_bitstream_version = BITSTREAM_VERSION

    # sizeof(SpeexHeader) in bytes as used by libspeex reference (fixed struct layout)
    # It is: 8 + 20 + 13 * 4 = 8 + 20 + 52 = 80
    header_size = 80

    reserved1 = 0
    reserved2 = 0

    # Pack the structure in little endian as the reference implementation does
    ints = [
        speex_version_id,
        header_size,
        rate,
        mode,
        mode_bitstream_version,
        nb_channels,
        bitrate,
        frame_size,
        vbr,
        frames_per_packet,
        extra_headers,
        reserved1,
        reserved2,
    ]

    body = struct.pack('<13i', *ints)
    packet = speex_string + speex_version + body

    # Optionally append padding bytes to simulate full packet buffers (some demuxers allow exact size)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        pad_len = rng.randrange(0, 8)
        packet += b"\x00" * pad_len

    return packet

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Occasionally generate multiple different valid headers concatenated to exercise length handling
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        count = rng.randrange(2, 4)
        parts = [build_header_packet(rng) for _ in range(count)]
        data = b"".join(parts)
        # Truncate to 4096 bytes if needed
        return data[:4096]
    else:
        return build_header_packet(rng)[:4096]
